description: AWS Well-Architected Framework best practices for production infrastructure

operational_excellence.title: Operational Excellence
practices: Use Infrastructure as Code (Terraform) for all resources — no manual console changes
Tag all resources with: Name, Environment, Project, ManagedBy, CostCenter
Enable CloudTrail across all regions for API audit logging
Use CloudWatch with structured logging and metric alarms
Implement runbooks and automated responses for common operational events
Use AWS Config for resource compliance monitoring

security.title: Security
practices: Enable MFA for all IAM users and root account
Use IAM roles with least-privilege policies — never share access keys
Enable AWS Security Hub for centralized security findings
Enable Amazon GuardDuty for threat detection
Encrypt all data at rest (S3, RDS, EBS with KMS)
Encrypt all data in transit (TLS 1.3 minimum)
Use AWS Secrets Manager or SSM Parameter Store for secrets
Enable VPC Flow Logs for network monitoring
Use AWS WAF for public-facing applications
Implement SCPs (Service Control Policies) in AWS Organizations

reliability.title: Reliability
practices: Deploy across multiple Availability Zones (minimum 2, prefer 3)
Use Auto Scaling groups for EC2 and managed node groups for EKS
Implement Circuit Breaker patterns for service dependencies
Use Multi-AZ for RDS and ElastiCache
Define and test Recovery Time Objectives (RTO) and Recovery Point Objectives (RPO)
Implement health checks at every layer (ALB, ECS, EKS)
Use Route 53 with health checks for DNS failover
Implement chaos engineering practices to test resilience

performance_efficiency.title: Performance Efficiency
practices: Use gp3 EBS volumes instead of gp2 for better price/performance
Use ALB over NLB unless TCP/UDP is specifically required
Implement CloudFront CDN for static assets and API responses
Use ElastiCache (Redis) for caching database queries
Right-size instances using AWS Compute Optimizer recommendations
Use Fargate Spot for non-critical workloads (up to 70% savings)
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration for large file uploads

cost_optimization.title: Cost Optimization
practices: Use Reserved Instances or Savings Plans for predictable workloads (30-60% savings)
Use a single NAT Gateway per VPC (not per AZ) for cost optimization in dev/staging
Implement S3 lifecycle policies to transition data to cheaper storage classes
Use Spot Instances for fault-tolerant batch workloads
Enable AWS Cost Explorer and set billing alarms
Tag resources for cost allocation and showback
Use AWS Budgets to enforce spending limits

sustainability.title: Sustainability
practices: Rightsize resources to avoid over-provisioning
Use graviton (ARM) instances where supported (20-40% cheaper and more efficient)
Shut down non-production environments after hours
Use Fargate Spot for interruptible workloads

eks_production_checklist: Kubernetes version within 2 minor versions of latest
Control plane endpoint with restricted access CIDRs
IRSA configured for all pods requiring AWS API access
Network policies implemented (Calico or AWS VPC CNI)
Pod security standards enforced (restricted or baseline)
Container images scanned for vulnerabilities (ECR scanning)
Horizontal Pod Autoscaler on all production deployments
Resource requests and limits on all containers
Multi-AZ node distribution via topology constraints
